findings.title: Proposition 4.4 permits finite-rank projections through a vacuous subspace condition
findings.source_claim: Projection classes in L(X)/SS(X) are equivalent to the biorthogonal basis under conditions alpha,beta,gamma; no infinite-dimensional range premise is stated.
findings.counterexample: U=X=ell_1, u_s=e_s, I_s x=x_s e_s, B=beta=C=1.
hypotheses: Condition beta follows exactly from disjoint coordinate supports
Every X_s is one-dimensional, so no Y has Y intersect X_s infinite-dimensional for all s; condition gamma is universally true over an empty class
findings.decisive_evidence: Every I_s is finite rank and strictly singular, hence its quotient class is zero, whereas ||u_s*||=1. Also I_1 is a nonzero element of [I_s] intersect SS(X), refuting directness. The unquotiented equivalence itself survives.
findings.proof: Report Section 3 supplies the full analytic hypothesis check and quotient contradiction.
findings.impact: The source explicitly does not use Proposition 4.4. The main construction uses the separate Proposition 4.1 and compact quotient. The demonstrated impact is local.

repair.verified: Add every X_s infinite-dimensional. Construct a basic-sequence span Y meeting all X_s infinitely with ||T|Y|| arbitrarily small for T strictly singular. Duality and gamma give beta/C ||sum lambda_s u_s*|| <= quotient norm <= B ||sum lambda_s u_s*||; identity independence follows from unused infinite-dimensional components.

problems.reasoning: For X=U=ell1 and I_s rank-one coordinate projections, alpha and beta hold exactly with B=1; gamma is true over an empty class of Y. Each nonzero I_s is finite rank and strictly singular, so its quotient class is zero, while its corresponding dual basis vector has norm1. The report correctly distinguishes the surviving unquotiented operator equivalence from the false quotient/direct-sum statement. The displayed duality argument then gives the exact quotient lower bound. Unused components prove identity independence.
